function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

**Java – A quick primer** | Topic | What you’ll find | |-------|------------------| | **What it is** | Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language designed with the philosophy “write once, run anywhere” (WORA). It was created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) and released publicly in 1995. | | **Core idea** | Code compiles into bytecode (`*.class` files), not native machine code. That bytecode runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which interprets or just‑in‑time compiles it to whatever platform’s CPU can understand. This makes Java programs portable across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android devices, embedded systems, servers, etc., without recompilation. | | **Key characteristics** | • Strongly typed & statically compiled.
• Automatic memory management via garbage collection.
• Rich standard library (java.lang.*, java.util.*, java.io.* …).
• Built‑in support for multithreading, networking, security APIs.
• Platform independence through JVM. | | **Typical use cases** | • Enterprise back‑end services (Spring Boot, Jakarta EE)
• Android mobile apps
• Desktop GUI applications (Swing/JavaFX)
• Embedded / IoT firmware (e.g., Raspberry Pi projects)
• Big data processing frameworks (Apache Hadoop, Spark)
• Game development (LibGDX, jMonkeyEngine) | | **Evolution timeline** | *1991–95*: JDK 1.0 → first public release.
*2002*: Java 2 Platform, Standard Edition (J2SE) becomes Java SE 5.0; generics, annotations added.
*2011*: Java 7 introduces try-with-resources, diamond operator.
*2014*: Java 8 brings lambda expressions, streams API, `Optional`.
*2019*: Java 15 adds sealed classes, records (preview).
*Ongoing*: New releases roughly every six months under the LTS cycle (Java 17, Java 21…). | | **Learning resources** | • Official docs: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/
• Interactive tutorials: Codecademy, Udemy, Coursera.
• Books: _Effective Java_ (Joshua Bloch), _Head First Java_. | --- ### Quick example ```java public class HelloWorld { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println("Hello, world!"); } } ``` Compile: ```bash javac HelloWorld.java # produces HelloWorld.class ``` Run: ```bash java HelloWorld # prints: Hello, world! ``` That single line of source turns into bytecode that the JVM executes on any supported OS. --- #### Bottom line Java remains one of the most widely used languages because its portability, robustness, vast ecosystem, and strong corporate backing make it suitable for everything from small utilities to massive distributed systems. Whether you're building web services, Android apps, or even smart appliances, Java offers a mature stack ready to handle your needs.
